description: Authored editorial decisions for the 12-word R6C prototype: which OEWN 2025 senses a Bangladeshi English learner needs, in which order, and the Ovidhan-written Bangla/English learner layer for every sense that V1 did not already carry. Every entry in selected/rejected must partition the full OEWN candidate set of the lemma (checked against the verified archive). Definitions are never written here: they are always the exact OEWN definition of the selected synset. The V1 sense (v1: true) is taken verbatim from the live V1 page and carries no learner text here. Records are generated from this file by scripts/dictionary-v2/migrate-v1.js; the audit report is generated by scripts/dictionary-v2/r6c.js.

words.risk_note: The two verb senses are close in meaning; they are kept apart because they use different frames (swarm + direction versus be swarming with) and different Bangla renderings.

v1_gap.description: V1 teaches only the noun (a swarm of bees). The verb is at least as common for learners (crowds swarm around a person; a place is swarming with insects or people) and was missing.

words.order_rationale: The V1 noun stays first: a swarm of insects is the concrete, basic meaning. The two verb uses follow, movement first and the 'full of' state second.

selected.reason: V1 primary sense: the core noun meaning (a swarm of bees). Retained verbatim.
Common verb use for crowds and insects moving in large numbers (fans swarmed around, people swarmed into the street).

learner.bangla_explanation: অনেক মানুষ, পোকা বা প্রাণী যখন একসঙ্গে দল বেঁধে কোনো দিকে ছুটে যায় বা কোনো জায়গায় ঢুকে পড়ে, সেই চলাকে ক্রিয়া হিসেবে swarm বলে। কোথায় বা কার দিকে যাচ্ছে বোঝাতে সাধারণত into, around বা out of-এর মতো শব্দ সঙ্গে বসে।
learner.example_en: Fans swarmed around the cricketer as soon as he stepped out of the hotel.
learner.example_bn: ক্রিকেটারটি হোটেল থেকে বের হতেই ভক্তরা দলবেঁধে তাঁকে ঘিরে ধরল।

selected.reason: Distinct, very common frame 'be swarming with': a place crowded or full of people, insects or animals.

learner.bangla_explanation: কোনো জায়গা যখন অনেক মানুষ, পোকা বা প্রাণীতে ঠাসা হয়ে থাকে, সেই অবস্থাকে swarm দিয়ে বোঝানো হয়। এখানে চলাফেরার চেয়ে জায়গাটির ভরে থাকাটাই আসল কথা; জায়গাটি যেন তাদের দিয়ে গিজগিজ করছে।
learner.example_en: By evening, the area around the village pond was swarming with mosquitoes.
learner.example_bn: সন্ধ্যা নামতেই গ্রামের পুকুরপাড় মশায় গিজগিজ করছিল।

usage_notes.text: এই অর্থে সাধারণ গঠন: be swarming with + যা দিয়ে জায়গাটি ভরা, যেমন swarming with tourists।

rejected.reason: A moving crowd: overlaps the retained noun sense and the selected movement verb, and its Bangla rendering (ঝাঁক/ভিড়) would duplicate them.

words.risk_note: 27 OEWN candidates; four senses are kept and 23 are rejected. The exclusion choices are judgement calls a reviewer may want to revisit. Challenge pass: the V1 Bangla example translation was unnatural ('প্রতিরাত পড়ে সে ভালো ফল করেছিল'); V2 now teaches an improved translation and keeps the exact V1 text only as the parity/traceability record (v1_revision), so V1 wording is not preferred merely for parity.

v1_gap.description: V1 teaches only the general 'having desirable qualities' adjective. It misses the three high-frequency frames good at (skill), a good person (moral character) and good for (beneficial), each of which needs a different Bangla word.

words.order_rationale: The V1 general sense stays first: it is the broadest and most frequent meaning. The skill, moral and beneficial senses follow in order of learner frequency.
words.more_than_three_justification: Challenge pass: all four selected senses are materially distinct and each is a high-frequency learner use. They differ in what is judged (quality of a thing, skill of a person, moral character, benefit to someone), in the Bangla word a learner needs (ভালো, দক্ষ/পটু, সৎ ও নীতিবান, উপকারী) and in the English frame (good + noun, good at, a good person, good for). Merging any two would hide a pattern. The other 23 candidates were re-read against these four and are redundant, idiomatic, narrow or nonstandard (see the per-candidate reasons).

selected.reason: V1 primary sense: the general 'desirable or positive qualities' meaning. OEWN definition and synset retained verbatim; the Bangla example translation is improved (v1_revision).

v1_revision.reason: The V1 Bangla example translation ('প্রতিরাত পড়ে সে ভালো ফল করেছিল') is unnatural Bangla ('প্রতিরাত' is not used with 'পড়ে' like this). V2 teaches the natural translation; the exact V1 text is kept only so V1 parity and traceability remain provable.

learner.example_bn: প্রতি রাতে পড়াশোনা করে সে ভালো ফল করেছিল।

selected.reason: The 'good at' skill sense: high frequency and a different Bangla word from the general sense.

learner.bangla_explanation: কোনো কাজ বা বিষয়ে যার জ্ঞান ও দক্ষতা আছে, তার সম্পর্কে good বলা হয়। এখানে good মানে 'ভালো মানুষ' নয়, বরং 'কাজটা ভালো পারে'।
learner.example_en: Tania is good at drawing, and her posters often win prizes at school.
learner.example_bn: তানিয়া ছবি আঁকায় পটু, তাই স্কুলে তার পোস্টার প্রায়ই পুরস্কার পায়।

selected.reason: A good person: moral character, clearly separate from quality or skill.

learner.bangla_explanation: যার চরিত্র ও আচরণ নৈতিকভাবে উঁচু মানের, অর্থাৎ যে ন্যায্য ও সৎ পথে চলে, তাকে good person বলা হয়। এখানে good দক্ষতা বা সুবিধা নয়, মানুষের নৈতিক গুণ বোঝায়।
learner.example_en: He is a good man; he returned the lost wallet with all the money still inside.
learner.example_bn: তিনি একজন সৎ মানুষ; হারানো মানিব্যাগটি তিনি সব টাকাসহ ফেরত দিয়েছিলেন।

selected.reason: The 'good for' beneficial sense (good for your health): the general OEWN synset for benefit, preferred over the narrower health-only synset.

learner.bangla_explanation: কোনো কিছু যখন কারও শরীর, মন বা জীবনের জন্য ভালো ফল বয়ে আনে, তখন সেটিকে তার জন্য good বলা হয়। এখানে লক্ষ্য হলো উপকার, কোনো জিনিসের মান নয়।
learner.example_en: Walking for half an hour every morning is good for your heart.
learner.example_bn: প্রতিদিন সকালে আধঘণ্টা হাঁটা তোমার হৃদযন্ত্রের জন্য উপকারী।

usage_notes.text: কীসে দক্ষ তা বোঝাতে good at + বিষয় বা -ing রূপ বসে, যেমন good at cooking।
কার উপকার হচ্ছে তা বোঝাতে good for + ব্যক্তি বা অঙ্গ বসে, যেমন good for children।

rejected.reason: Trade/commerce noun (a commodity); technical and not what learners mean by 'good'.
Abstract noun counterpart of the selected moral-character sense (goodness); low independent learner value.
Abstract philosophical noun ('the good'); low learner value.
Idiomatic noun use ('for your own good', 'what is the good of'); overlaps the selected beneficial sense and is better taught as a phrase.
Quantifier use ('a good mile'); idiomatic and rare for learners.
Close-relationship reading ('a good friend'): learners understand it from the general sense (ভালো বন্ধু); the 'close/intimate' nuance is better taught with 'close friend'.
Narrow intensifier use ('a good cleaning'); low priority.
Vague 'generally admired' gloss ('good taste'); overlaps the general V1 sense.
Validity sense ('a warranty good for two years'); administrative and rare for general learners.
Pattern 'it is a good thing that'; covered by the general V1 sense.
Food-freshness use ('the milk is still good'): real but a narrow collocation of the general 'acceptable condition' meaning, and not a distinct pattern learners need to be taught.
Not forged (counterfeit money); specialist and rare.
Duplicates the selected moral sense (02052395-a); the selected synset is the richer one.
Near-duplicate of the selected beneficial sense; 'good for health' is shown in that sense's usage.
Excellent physical condition ('good teeth'); covered by the general V1 sense.
Vague 'appealing to the mind' gloss ('good music'); covered by the general V1 sense.

Agreeable or pleasing ('a good time', 'good weather'): frequent, but it is the general 'desirable' meaning applied to experiences; the OEWN gloss is vague and it needs no different English frame or Bangla word (ভালো).
Suitability use ('a good time to plant'); covered by the general V1 sense.
Capable of pleasing ('good looks'); narrow, collocation-driven.
Formal 'deserving of esteem' cluster ('a good name'); low learner frequency.
Financially safe ('a good investment'); finance-specific.
OEWN itself marks this adverb as a nonstandard dialectal variant of 'well'; not taught as standard.
Informal intensifier ('beat him good'); informal and nonstandard.

v1_gap.description: None. V1 already carries the only general-English sense (extreme confusion and disorder). The other two OEWN senses are a physics term and a mythological term.

words.order_rationale: Single sense; the V1 sense is retained unchanged.

selected.reason: V1 primary sense and the only general-English sense. Retained verbatim.

rejected.reason: Physics/mathematics term (chaos theory); technical, not a learner sense.
Cosmogony/mythology sense (the formless state before creation); literary and rare.

words.risk_note: Challenge pass: both OEWN action senses were added after re-reading all three candidates. The first rejection reason ('derivational, better taught with the verb') was withdrawn because the act senses are a different, genuinely used pattern (designation of X as Y). OEWN has no separate 'position/post' synset: the title sense (V1) is the one that covers an official title or name, and the position idea is carried by the appointment sense.

v1_gap.description: V1 teaches only the title/name noun (পদবি), which is the dominant sense on forms and job documents. It misses the two action uses that appear in formal and news English: appointing someone to a post ('her designation as director') and officially naming or declaring something ('the designation of the fort as a protected site').

words.order_rationale: The V1 title/name sense stays first: it is the use Bangladeshi learners meet most (forms, job letters). The appointment sense follows because it also concerns offices and posts, then the general act of officially designating a place or thing.

selected.reason: V1 primary sense: the title/name meaning (an official title or name by which someone or something is called and classified) that Bangladeshi learners meet on forms and job documents. Retained verbatim.

The act of putting a person into a non-elective post (designation as director). Materially distinct from the title noun: it names an action done to a person, with a different Bangla word (নিয়োগ, মনোনয়ন).

learner.bangla_explanation: কাউকে নির্বাচন ছাড়াই কোনো পদে বসানো বা মনোনীত করার কাজকে designation বলে। এখানে designation পদবির নাম নয়, বরং ব্যক্তিটিকে সেই পদে দেওয়ার কাজ; তাই সাধারণত designation as + পদ আকারে বসে।
learner.example_en: The ministry confirmed her designation as the new project director last week.
learner.example_bn: মন্ত্রণালয় গত সপ্তাহে প্রকল্পের নতুন পরিচালক হিসেবে তাঁর নিয়োগ নিশ্চিত করেছে।

selected.reason: The act of designating or identifying something (designation of a place as protected). Distinct from both the title noun and the person-appointment sense: its object is a thing or place, with its own Bangla rendering (ঘোষণা, চিহ্নিতকরণ).

learner.bangla_explanation: কোনো জায়গা, জিনিস বা বিষয়কে আনুষ্ঠানিকভাবে কোনো নাম বা মর্যাদা দিয়ে চিহ্নিত করার কাজকে designation বলে। যেমন কোনো এলাকাকে সংরক্ষিত স্থান হিসেবে ঘোষণা করা। এখানে শব্দটি একটি কাজের নাম, কোনো নামের বা পদের নয়।
learner.example_en: The government's designation of the old fort as a protected site was welcomed by historians.
learner.example_bn: পুরোনো দুর্গটিকে সংরক্ষিত স্থান হিসেবে সরকারের ঘোষণাকে ইতিহাসবিদরা স্বাগত জানালেন।

v1_gap.description: None. V1 carries the only learner-relevant sense (the personality noun). The verb senses are technical.

words.order_rationale: Single sense; the V1 sense is retained unchanged.

selected.reason: V1 primary sense and the only learner-relevant sense. Retained verbatim.

rejected.reason: Rare psychological/technical verb (turn inward); not used in everyday learner English.
Anatomical/biological verb (fold inwards, invaginate); technical.

words.risk_note: Challenge pass: the strong/sturdy/durable physical sense was reconsidered and added; the earlier 'stay within three' reason was removed because the three-sense target is not a limit. Eight of twelve candidates remain rejected, each on its own merits.
words.more_than_three_justification: Challenge pass: 'tough' has four common, materially distinct learner senses with four different Bangla renderings and four different things being described: a hard task or situation (কঠিন), a person's temperament (কঠোর ও শক্ত মনের), a well-made object (মজবুত, টেকসই) and food that is hard to chew (শক্ত, চিবানো কঠিন). The sturdy/durable sense is supported by OEWN synset 00714724-a ('substantially made or constructed'; sturdy, tough) and is not covered by any other selected sense.

v1_gap.description: V1 teaches only 'difficult / demanding'. It misses the personality sense (a tough, unsentimental person), the strong/durable physical sense (tough boots, tough fabric) and the food sense (tough meat), all common and with different Bangla words.

words.order_rationale: The V1 'difficult' sense stays first: it is the most frequent use (a tough exam, a tough decision). The personality sense follows, then the strong/durable object sense, then the food sense.

selected.reason: V1 primary sense: difficult or demanding. Retained verbatim.
A tough person: not gentle or sentimental. Different from 'difficult' and common in everyday English.

learner.bangla_explanation: যে মানুষ কোমল স্বভাবের নয় এবং সহজে আবেগে গলে না, তাকে tough বলা হয়। এখানে tough গায়ের জোর নয়, স্বভাব ও মনোভাবের কঠোরতা বোঝায়।
learner.example_en: Our coach is tough and never accepts excuses, even from his best players.
learner.example_bn: আমাদের কোচ কঠোর মানুষ; সেরা খেলোয়াড়দের কাছ থেকেও তিনি কোনো অজুহাত মানেন না।

selected.reason: Strong, durable, well-made things (tough boots, tough fabric). Materially distinct from difficulty, temperament and food texture; OEWN lists tough with 'sturdy' in this synset.

learner.bangla_explanation: কোনো জিনিস এমনভাবে বানানো যে সহজে ভাঙে না বা ছিঁড়ে যায় না এবং কঠিন ব্যবহারেও টিকে থাকে, তাকে tough বলা হয়। কাপড়, জুতা বা যন্ত্রের শক্তপোক্ত গঠনই এখানে মূল কথা; কাজ কঠিন হওয়া বা মাংস শক্ত হওয়া নয়।
learner.example_en: She bought tough rubber boots that last through the whole monsoon.
learner.example_bn: সে এমন মজবুত রাবারের বুট কিনেছে, যা পুরো বর্ষা টিকে যায়।

selected.reason: Tough meat: resistant to cutting or chewing. A classic learner sense that no other selected sense covers.

learner.bangla_explanation: কোনো খাবার, বিশেষ করে মাংস, এমন শক্ত যে কাটতে বা চিবাতে কষ্ট হয়, তাকে tough বলা হয়। এখানে 'কঠিন' মানে পরিশ্রমসাধ্য নয়, বরং জিনিসটির নিজের গঠনই শক্ত।
learner.example_en: The meat was too tough to chew, so the children left it on their plates.
learner.example_bn: মাংসটা এত শক্ত ছিল যে চিবানো যাচ্ছিল না, তাই বাচ্চারা সেটা প্লেটেই রেখে দিল।

rejected.reason: Informal noun for a cruel, brutal person; overlaps the personality sense and is rare as a noun.
Slang noun for a violent young criminal; informal and potentially stigmatising.
Boxing-specific noun (a street fighter).
OEWN marks this as an occasional colloquial use for 'bad' (feeling unwell); not a standard learner sense.
Hard to comprehend or solve ('a tough question'): the V1 'difficult' sense and its exam example already teach this use, and both render as কঠিন; not materially distinct.
Unfortunate or hard to bear ('tough luck', 'a tough break'): the hardship meaning is already in the V1 sense ('a tough life'); the fixed expressions are better taught as phrases.
Physically toughened (tough soles of the feet); narrow and rare.
Violent and lawless (tough street gangs); overlaps the personality sense and risks stereotyping.

words.risk_note: Two OEWN senses (an 'uncivilized' people / without civilizing influences) are deliberately excluded because they are dated and derogatory. The exclusion is a sensitivity decision, not a frequency one. Challenge pass: the 'criticize harshly' verb was re-compared with every other candidate and kept (see its selection reason).

v1_gap.description: V1 teaches only the adjective (cruel, violent). The verb uses (to attack brutally; to criticize harshly) are common in news English and were missing.

words.order_rationale: The V1 adjective stays first. The physical-attack verb follows because it is the verb counterpart of the V1 meaning; the figurative criticism verb comes last.

selected.reason: V1 primary sense: cruel, violent (adjective). Retained verbatim.
Verb: to attack brutally and fiercely (a dog savaged a child). Common in news English and absent from V1.

learner.bangla_explanation: কেউ বা কোনো প্রাণী যখন নির্মম ও প্রচণ্ড হিংস্রতায় অন্যকে আক্রমণ করে গুরুতর আঘাত করে, সেই কাজকে ক্রিয়া হিসেবে savage বলে। এখানে savage বিশেষণ নয়, ক্রিয়া; এর অতীত রূপ savaged।
learner.example_en: A stray dog savaged the boy before the neighbours drove it away.
learner.example_bn: প্রতিবেশীরা তাড়িয়ে দেওয়ার আগে একটি পথের কুকুর ছেলেটির ওপর হিংস্রভাবে ঝাঁপিয়ে পড়েছিল।

selected.reason: Challenge pass, kept: verb 'criticize harshly' (critics savaged the film). Compared with every other modern candidate (the V1 cruelty adjective, the attack verb, the wild/menacing and fierce-intensity adjectives), it is the only one that adds a distinct meaning, a distinct English frame (savage + a work, person or decision) and a distinct Bangla rendering. It is a standard, frequent usage in reviews and news, so it earns learner-facing inclusion.

learner.bangla_explanation: গায়ে হাত না তুলে বরং কোনো সিনেমা, বই, নেতা বা সিদ্ধান্তকে অত্যন্ত তীব্র ও নির্মম ভাষায় সমালোচনা করাকে savage বলা হয়। শারীরিক আক্রমণ নয়, কথার আঘাতই এখানে বিষয়।
learner.example_en: Critics savaged the film, calling it dull and badly written.
learner.example_bn: সমালোচকেরা সিনেমাটির কড়া সমালোচনা করে একে একঘেয়ে আর খারাপভাবে লেখা বললেন।

rejected.reason: Rare noun for a cruelly rapacious person; low learner frequency.
Dated, derogatory noun for a member of an 'uncivilized' people; deliberately not taught.
